newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel forex reserves rise to record $10.262 bln.
newsitem.headline: Israel forex reserves rise to record $10.262 bln.

text.p: Israel's foreign currency reserves at the end of September rose by $739 million to a record $10.262 billion, the Bank of Israel said.
The Bank of Israel attributed the rise to its market interventions during the month as well as to government transfers of foreign currency from abroad.
The central bank bought foreign currency in September to prevent the shekel from appreciating beyond the band in which it is allowed to trade.

The bank said in a statement that the sale of foreign currency by the private sector was mainly the result of an increase in loans of foreign currency loans taken by the private sector from Israeli commercial banks.
The Bank of Israel said it used other monetary tools to offset the interventions and prevent money supply from expanding.
